sections.text_helper: Section 35.5.18 "Delayed break" in chapter 35 (General purpose timers (TIM15/TIM16/TIM17)), RM0522 Rev 1, page 1382.
sections.section_content:
In Neutral-Point Clamped (NPC) multilevel converter topology, a break strategy with
immediate outputs shut-down is not suitable, as it may damage the power switches with
excessive voltage levels.
The delayed break features provide 2 options delaying the response to a break event, and
implement a safe shut-down sequence.
BKMx[1:0] and BKMxN[1:0] bitfields in TIM_MPR1 provides 3 options for each
complementary outputs (tim_oc1/tim_oc1n to tim_oc2/tim_oc2n), as show on Figure511
below:
– BKM[1:0] = 00: the break response is immediate
– BKM[1:0] = 01: Delayed 1 break. The break response is delayed with a delay
defined in the DBK1[7:0] bitfield of the TIM_MPR2 register
– BKM[1:0] = 10: Delayed 2 break. The break response is delayed with a delay
defined in the DBK2[7:0] bitfield of the TIM_MPR2 register
[Figure 511. Immediate break and Delayed 1/2 break modes]
The delayed break mode is triggered when:
• A break event occurs
• The MOE bit is reset
• When the microcontroller enters debug mode with DBG_TIMx_STOP=1
When delayed break mode is triggered, the MOE bit is immediately cleared, and cannot be
set during the delayed break duration. In bidirectional break mode, the break output is reset
immediately to indicate the delayed break start to external components. Once the longest of
the 2 delays is over, the deadtime generator is enabled to prevent any deadtime violation if
OISx/OISxN bits are set.
If the tim_ocx/tim_ocxn signal is reset before the end of the delayed break (due to a
compare match in PWM mode, typically), the signal is not maintained during the full delayed
break period, to maintain the duty cycle, as shown on Figure512 below. Still, the Delayed
break circuitry guarantees that the tim_ocx/tim_ocxn signals cannot be set again once the
break event occurred.
[Figure 512. Pulse termination during delayed break]

The Figure513 depicts the behavior when the deadtime generator is enabled, for the 3
cases:
– Delayed break triggered when tim_ocx is set
– Delayed break triggered when tim_ocxn is set
– Delayed break triggered during deadtime interval
[Figure 513. Delayed break with deadtime insertion]
The delay programming is identical to deadtime generator’s, with 2 user-programmable
durations in the TIM_MPR2 register: DBK1[7:0] bitfield for the Delayed 1 break and
DBK2[7:0] bitfield for the Delayed 2 break.
DBK1[7:0] and DBK2[7:0] bitfields are preloaded: they can be changed during timer
operation, and the new value is transferred to the active register when an update event
occurs.
The bits coding for tDTG selection are not preloaded.
It is thus recommended to update only the least significant bits to have the expected
duration value:
• DBKx[6:0] if DBKx[7]=0
• DBKx[5:0] if DBKx[7:6]=10
• DBKx[4:0] if DBKx[7:5]=110or111
The BKMx[1:0] and BKMxN[1:0] bits are static, they can only be modified when the counter
is stopped (CEN=0 in TIM_CR1).
The content of the TIM_MPR1 and TIM_MPR2 register can be write protected using the
LOCK[1:0] bits in the TIM_BDTR register.
